source_text: Καὶ τί δεῖ λέγειν περὶ τῶν μηδενὶ ζώῳ πρὸς τροφὴν ἀποκληρωθέντων σωμάτων, μόνην δὲ τὴν εἰς γῆν γῆν ταφὴν ἐπὶ τιμῇ τῆς φύσεως μεμοιραμένων, ὅπου γε μηδ᾿ ἄλλο τι τῶν ζώων τοῖς ἐκ τοῦ αὐτοῦ εἴδους εἰς τροφὴν ἀπεκλήρωσεν ὁ ποιήσας, κἂν ἐν ἄλλοις τισὶ τῶν ἑτερογενῶν τροφὴ γίνηται κατὰ φύσιν; Εἰ μὲν οὖν ἔχουσι δεικνύναι σάρκας ἀνθρώπων ἀνθρώποις εἰς βρῶσιν ἀποκληρωθείσας, οὐδὲν κωλύσει τὰς ἀλληλοφαγίας εἶναι κατὰ φύσιν, ὥσπερ ἄλλο τι τῶν τῇ φύσει συγκεχωρημένων, καὶ τούς γε τὰ τοιαῦτα λέγειν τολμῶντας τοῖς τῶν φιλτάτων ἐντρυφᾶν σώμασιν, ὡς οἰκειοτέροις, ἢ καὶ τοὺς εὐνουστάτους σφίσι τούτοις αὐτοῖς ἑστιᾶν. Εἰ δὲ τοῦτο μὲν οὐδ᾿ εἰπεῖν εὐαγές, τὸ δὲ σαρκῶν ἀνθρώπων ἀνθρώπους μετασχεῖν ἔχθιστόν τι καὶ παμμίαρον καὶ πάσης ἐκθέσμου καὶ παρὰ φύσιν βρώσεως ἢ πράξεως ἐναγέστερον, τὸ δὲ παρὰ φύσιν οὐκ ἄν ποτε χωρήσειεν εἰς τροφὴν τοῖς ταύτης δεομένοις μέρεσι καὶ μορίοις, τὸ δὲ μὴ χωροῦν εἰς τροφὴν οὐκ ἂν ἑνωθείη τούτοις ἃ μηδὲ τρέφειν πέφυκεν, οὐδὲ τὰ τῶν ἀνθρώπων σώματα συγκριθείη ποτ᾿ ἂν τοῖς ὁμοίοις σώμασιν, οἷς ἐστιν εἰς τροφὴν παρὰ φύσιν, κἂν πολλάκις διὰ τῆς τούτων ἴῃ γαστρὸς κατά τινα πικροτάτην συμφοράν· ἀποχωροῦντα δὲ τῆς θρεπτικῆς δυνάμεως, καὶ σκιδνάμενα πρὸς ἐκεῖνα πάλιν ἐξ ὧν τὴν πρώτην ἔσχε σύστασιν, ἑνοῦται μὲν τούτοις ἐφ᾿ ὅσον ἂν ἕκαστον τύχῃ χρόνον· ἐκεῖθεν δὲ διακριθέντα πάλιν σοφίᾳ καὶ δυνάμει τοῦ πᾶσαν ζώου φύσιν σὺν ταῖς οἰκείαις δυνάμεσι συγκρίναντος ἑνοῦται προσφυῶς ἕκαστον ἑκάστῳ, κἂν πυρὶ καυθῇ, κἂν ὕδατι κατασαπῇ, κἂν ὑπὸ θηρίων ἢ τῶν ἐπιτυχόντων ζώων καταδαπανηθῇ, κἂν τοῦ παντὸς σώματος ἐκκοπὲν προδιαλυθῇ τῶν ἄλλων μερῶν· ἑνωθέντα δὲ πάλιν ἀλλήλοις τὴν αὐτὴν ἴσχει χώραν πρὸς τὴν τοῦ αὐτοῦ σώματος ἁρμονίαν τε καὶ σύστασιν καὶ τὴν τοῦ νεκρωθέντος ἢ καὶ πάντη διαλυθέντος ἀνάστασιν καὶ ζωήν. Ταῦτα μὲν οὖν ἐπὶ πλεῖον μηκύνειν οὐκ εὔκαιρον· ὁμολογουμένην γὰρ ἔχει τὴν ἐπίκρισιν, τοῖς γε μὴ μιξοθήροις.
thought_title: What is against nature cannot become food or be united to a body
orientation: Athenagoras is answering the objection that human bodies eaten by other humans or animals could be blended with those bodies, by arguing that what is against nature can never become true food or be united to a body.
pass_a_gloss: And why is it necessary to speak about the bodies that have been allotted to no animal for food, but have received only burial in earth, earth, in honor of nature, since indeed the maker allotted no other of the animals to those of the same kind for food, even if among certain others of the different kinds food comes to be according to nature? If then they can show that human flesh has been allotted to humans for eating, nothing will prevent mutual eating from being according to nature, just as any other of the things conceded to nature, and indeed those who dare to say such things from feasting on the bodies of their dearest ones, as being more their own, or even from entertaining their most loyal friends with these very things. But if to say this is not even holy, and for humans to share in human flesh is something most hateful and utterly defiled and more accursed than every lawless and against-nature eating or act, and what is against nature would never pass into food for the parts and members that need it, and what does not pass into food would never be united to those things which it is not its nature to nourish, then neither would the bodies of humans ever be blended with bodies like them, for which it is food against nature, even if often through their stomach it goes by some most bitter misfortune; but departing from the nourishing power, and being scattered again to those things from which it first had its composition, it is united to these for as long a time as each happens to be; and from there being separated again by the wisdom and power of the one who composed every nature of animal with its proper powers, each is united fittingly to each, even if it is burned by fire, even if it rots away in water, even if it is consumed by wild beasts or by whatever animals happen upon it, even if cut off from the whole body it is dissolved before the other parts; and being united again to one another it holds the same place for the harmony and composition of the same body and the resurrection and life of the one who has died or even been completely dissolved. To prolong these matters further is not opportune; for it has an agreed judgment, at least for those who are not beast-mixed.

choices.why: The verb conveys a fixed assignment by the maker; 'allotted' preserves the sense of a determined portion rather than a general giving.
The compound means eating one another; 'mutual eating' keeps the reciprocal force without importing modern 'cannibalism' as a technical term.
The prefix παν- intensifies the pollution; 'utterly defiled' conveys the total impurity rather than a weaker 'unclean.'
The verb means to make room for or be received into; 'pass into food' captures the idea of being admitted as nourishment.
The verb means to combine or mix together; 'blended' preserves the physical mixing sense central to the objection being answered.
The rare compound means mixed with beasts; a literal rendering keeps the insulting force aimed at those who blur human and animal nature.

pass_b_english: And why should I speak of bodies that have been allotted to no animal as food, but have received burial in the earth alone as their portion, in honor of nature? For the Maker has not allotted to any animal another animal of the same kind as food, even if among some of the different kinds one becomes food according to nature. If, then, they can show that human flesh has been allotted to humans for eating, nothing will prevent mutual eating from being according to nature, just like any other thing permitted by nature—and nothing will prevent those who dare to say such things from feasting on the bodies of their dearest ones as more fitting food, or even from feasting their closest friends with these very things. But if it is not even lawful to say this, and if for humans to share in human flesh is something most hateful, utterly defiled, and more accursed than every unlawful and unnatural eating or act, and if what is contrary to nature could never pass into food for the parts and members that need it, and if what does not pass into food could never be united to those things it is not naturally able to nourish, then neither could the bodies of humans ever be blended with bodies like them, for which they are food contrary to nature—even if through some most bitter misfortune they often pass through the stomach of these. Departing from the nourishing power and being scattered again toward those things from which they had their first composition, they are united to them for whatever time each happens to last. But when they are separated from there again, by the wisdom and power of the One who blended every animal nature with its proper powers, each is united fittingly to each—whether burned by fire, rotted away by water, consumed by beasts or by whatever animals happen upon them, or a part cut off from the whole body and dissolved before the other parts. And when they are united again to one another, they hold the same place for the harmony and composition of the same body, and for the resurrection and life of the one who has died or been completely dissolved. It is not the right time to prolong these matters further, for the judgment is agreed upon—at least by those who are not half-beasts.

problems.quote: entertaining their closest friends with themselves
problems.source_quote: τοὺς εὐνουστάτους σφίσι τούτοις αὐτοῖς ἑστιᾶν
problems.why: Greek means 'feasting their closest friends with these very things' (the flesh), not 'with themselves.'
problems.fix: or even from feasting their closest friends with these very things
problems.ruling: τούτοις αὐτοῖς ('these very things,' the flesh) is mistranslated as 'with themselves,' misleading the reader.

problems.why: τούτων refers to the animals', not 'their' (humans'); 'their stomach' misidentifies whose stomach.
problems.ruling: τούτων refers to ὁμοίοις σώμασιν (the like bodies eaten), not the humans eating; 'their stomach' misidentifies referent.

edits.old: or even from entertaining their closest friends with themselves.
edits.new: or even from feasting their closest friends with these very things.

edits.old: they often pass through their stomach.
edits.new: they often pass through the stomach of these.

problems.quote: the Maker has not allotted any other animal to those of the same kind as food
problems.source_quote: μηδ᾿ ἄλλο τι τῶν ζώων τοῖς ἐκ τοῦ αὐτοῦ εἴδους εἰς τροφὴν ἀπεκλήρωσεν ὁ ποιήσας
problems.why: Reverses agency: God has not allotted any other animal of the same species to any animal as food (not 'to those of the same kind').
problems.fix: the Maker has not allotted to any animal another animal of the same kind as food
problems.ruling: τοῖς ἐκ τοῦ αὐτοῦ εἴδους = 'those of same kind'; English 'any other animal to those of same kind' correctly conveys no same-species predation.

problems.quote: nothing will prevent those who dare to say such things from feasting on the bodies of their dearest ones as more fitting, or even from feasting their closest friends with these very things
problems.source_quote: καὶ τούς γε τὰ τοιαῦτα λέγειν τολμῶντας τοῖς τῶν φιλτάτων ἐντρυφᾶν σώμασιν, ὡς οἰκειοτέροις, ἢ καὶ τοὺς εὐνουστάτους σφίσι τούτοις αὐτοῖς ἑστιᾶν
problems.why: Misreads syntax: 'τοῖς...σώμασιν, ὡς οἰκειοτέροις' means 'on the bodies of their dearest ones as more fitting [food]', but 'ἑστιᾶν' takes double accusative: 'to feast their closest friends on these very things', not 'feast their closest friends with these very things'.
problems.fix: from feasting on the bodies of their dearest ones as more fitting food, or even from feasting their closest friends on these very things
problems.ruling: ἑστιᾶν takes double accusative: 'feast friends on these things'; 'with' misleads reader about cannibalistic hosting.

edits.old: the Maker has not allotted any other animal to those of the same kind as food
edits.new: the Maker has not allotted to any animal another animal of the same kind as food

edits.old: from feasting on the bodies of their dearest ones as more fitting, or even from feasting their closest friends with these very things
edits.new: from feasting on the bodies of their dearest ones as more fitting food, or even from feasting their closest friends on these very things

problems.quote: nothing will prevent those who dare to say such things from feasting on the bodies of their dearest ones as more fitting food, or even from feasting their closest friends on these very things
problems.source_quote: τούς γε τὰ τοιαῦτα λέγειν τολμῶντας τοῖς τῶν φιλτάτων ἐντρυφᾶν σώμασιν, ὡς οἰκειοτέροις, ἢ καὶ τοὺς εὐνουστάτους σφίσι τούτοις αὐτοῖς ἑστιᾶν
problems.why: Second clause: they feast their closest friends WITH these things, not 'on' them; both are cannibal feasts
problems.fix: or even from feasting their closest friends with these very things
problems.ruling: τοὺς εὐνουστάτους...ἑστιᾶν = 'feast closest friends ON these things'; English 'feasting friends on' means serving them, reversing cannibalism point.

problems.quote: cut off from the whole body and dissolved before the other parts
problems.source_quote: κἂν τοῦ παντὸς σώματος ἐκκοπὲν προδιαλυθῇ τῶν ἄλλων μερῶν
problems.why: ἐκκοπὲν is neuter singular: 'a part cut off from the whole body', not the body cut off
problems.fix: even if a part cut off from the whole body is dissolved before the other parts
problems.ruling: ἐκκοπὲν is neuter singular participle: 'a part cut off from whole body'; English 'cut off from whole body' implies body is cut, changing meaning.

edits.old: or even from feasting their closest friends on these very things
edits.new: or even from feasting their closest friends with these very things

edits.old: or cut off from the whole body and dissolved before the other parts
edits.new: or a part cut off from the whole body and dissolved before the other parts

fixed: Changed 'on these very things' to 'with these very things' to reflect the Greek instrumental sense of feasting friends with the bodies.
Changed 'cut off from the whole body' to 'a part cut off from the whole body' to reflect the neuter singular participle ἐκκοπὲν referring to a part, not the whole body.

fixed.note: μιξοθήροις = half-beasts (ANF 'semi-brutes'); 'beast-mixed' is not English. Minor readability fix; proposed fix offers two alternatives joined by 'or'.

dismissed.quote: for which they are food contrary to nature
dismissed.why: Relative pronoun refers to the humans eating, not the bodies: 'by those for whom it is food contrary to nature'.
dismissed.note: οἷς refers to the 'like bodies' (other humans) for whom human bodies are unnatural food; English 'bodies like them, for which they are food' already says that.
